question.problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}]^{T}$ be a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2}+3{X}_{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2}+3{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =2-2-3 \\  & =-3,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 \\ 5 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =9-5+60 \\  & =64.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(-3,64).
$$
